mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases but SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate indicates labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises but SPX returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts suggests reduced demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines but SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing industrial production growth indicates supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth slows but SPX returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales and housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both RSAFS and HOUST rise but SPX 60-day returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing employment growth indicates labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS growth slows but SPX returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate alongside low unemployment suggests tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is high and UNRATE is low but SPX returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth indicates weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth slows but SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 40% of the time.
